summary: Describes TCP Cookie Transactions, an experimental TCP extension meant to resist connection spoofing and resource exhaustion by letting a server avoid keeping state during the initial handshake. The cookie exchange can carry limited data. It is historic and was replaced by RFC 7805.

eli5.summary: A server usually must remember everyone who knocks, even fakers. This idea made the knocker carry a token so the server did not need to remember. It is now historic and was replaced by RFC 7805.

questions: tcp syn flood defense with cookies
